cues: In a defining clause you may drop the pronoun when it is the object: this is the book I told you about; but never when it is the subject.
That is preferred after superlatives and after all, only and nothing.
A preposition may go before whom or which, or at the end, but never before that.
And a relative clause can often shrink to a participle: the boy standing at the gate; the letter written by him.
